title: Maximum Number of Consecutive Values You Can Make
summary: Given an array of coin values, determine the longest sequence of consecutive integer values that can be formed by summing any subset of these coins, starting from 0.
statement: Given an array of coin values, determine the longest sequence of consecutive integer values that can be formed by summing any subset of these coins, starting from 0. Note that duplicate coin values are allowed.
constraints: Each positive coin may be used at most once; duplicate values are separate coins.
Return how many consecutive sums beginning with zero are constructible.
hints: Maintain the first value that is not yet constructible.
Sort coins; a coin no larger than reach extends the constructible interval.
Start reach at one and add each usable coin until a gap appears.
If sums through reach-1 exist, adding coin<=reach covers continuously through reach+coin-1; coin>reach can never fill reach.
editorial: If sums through reach-1 exist, adding coin<=reach covers continuously through reach+coin-1; coin>reach can never fill reach.

tests.explanation: Only zero and one are constructible before the gap at two, so return two.
Every value zero through seven is constructible, so return eight.
